findings.passage: But when you look at in practice, the (state) bill, as written in House Bill 1300 was so restrictive on the type of ID that could have been used, that it wouldn’t have even allowed my Senate ID to count as a state ID.
findings.note: Quoted by The Epoch Times (reporter Beth Brelje) while he was a U.S. Senate candidate: on the kinds of ID accepted under House Bill 1300 (2021).

findings.passage: Do I think you could craft a fairer version of a voter ID bill? Probably could. But 1300 just doesn’t do that. Secondly, I think it’s a solution in search of a problem. We don’t have a problem of people showing up in person and impersonating someone else to vote. That just is not really a systemic problem. There’s no evidence that is a systemic problem anywhere.
findings.note: Quoted by The Epoch Times: says a fairer voter ID bill could be written, says HB 1300 is not it, and says in-person impersonation is not a systemic problem.

findings.passage: We have seen efforts to disenfranchise voters by advancing burdensome and duplicative Voter ID requirements before. This is Jim Crow 2.0.
findings.note: Quote credited to him in a 2021 press release on his own site, issued at an event about House Bill 1300 (which includes voter ID and mail-ballot ID rules).
